μήτηρ μὲν, ἐπειδὴ ὁ διδάξας με, δι' αὐτῆς με γεγέν νηκεν, ὡς Παῦλος διὰ τοῦ
Εὐαγγελίου Γαλάτας· γυνὴ δὲ, ὅτι συνοῦσά μοι τίκτει τὰς ἀρετὰς καὶ δόγματα ὀρθά·
εἴ γε ἡ σοφία ἀνδρὶ τίκτει φρόνησιν· ἀδελφὴ, ὅτι ἐγώ τε καὶ αὕτη ἐκ τοῦ ἑνὸς
γεγόναμεν Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρός· Εἶπον γὰρ, φησὶ, τὴν σοφίαν, σὴν ἀδελ φὴν εἶναι. Ἡ
χάρις καὶ ἡ φιλία ἐλευθεροῖ· ἡ δὲ ἀρετὴ καὶ γνῶσις ἐλευθεροῦσι ψυχὴν λογικήν· ἡ
χάρις γὰρ καὶ ἡ φιλία, ἀρετὴ καὶ γνῶσίς ἐστιν· εἰ δὲ ἔλαφος ἐκ τῆς φιλίας, ὁ πῶλος
ἐκ τῶν χαρίτων γεννᾶται· ἡ οὖν ἔλαφός ἐστι τῆς θεωρίας σύμβολον· ὁ δὲ πῶλος, τῆς
ἀπαθείας· ἡ μὲν γὰρ, ἐξ ἀρετῶν· ἡ δὲ, ἐκ τῆς γνώσεως γίνεσθαι πέφυκεν. –Ἡ μὲν

pass_a_gloss: sleep is the active sin of the psyche; drowse is the first impure thought gathered in the psyche; post-drowse is the inclination toward worse things; for this reason the law forbids sleep, the Gospel forbids drowse, if the former cuts off active sin, the latter the first evil thought gathered by reason; it was said to the ancients, do not be angry; but I say to you, do not be provoked; note here that the harmonious motion of the ant’s nature is called wisdom; for the wiser of the wise is called wiser; how then is it not under a master, if all things are slaves of God? or perhaps God is called master in two ways, as creator and as known; for this reason Paul writes: now having been freed from sin, and having been enslaved to God (obviously according to arete and knowing), you have your fruit for sanctification, and the end eternal life; but if the ant, being irrational, lacks share in such end and knowing, it is clear that it is also free from such servitude; well then it is said that the ant is not under master according to this lordship; but again it is said to be under lordship, under God, as under creator; through the ant Solomon seems to inscribe for us the practical way; through the fleecing, the theory. Youth and the divine covenant forgotten; forgetfulness and neglect are secondary to knowing acquisition; as health’s ultimate illness and life’s secondary death; simultaneously, the same knowing is called mother, wife, and sister since the teacher begets through it, as Paul says of the Gospel to the Galatians; she is wife since she bears virtues and correct teachings with me, if wisdom begets prudence in a man; she is sister since we both come from the one God and Father; I said, he says, that wisdom is your sister; grace and friendship liberate; arete and knowing liberate the rational psyche; for grace and friendship are arete and knowing; if the hind comes from friendship, the colt comes from graces; for this reason the hind is the symbol of theory; the colt, of apathy; for the one is from virtues, the other from knowing; it comes to pass naturally; the hind is the symbol of theory, of incorporeal things and of God’s knowing; friendship is the love toward God and neighbor; the colt is apathy; theory concerning God’s knowing naturally arises from virtues; love comes to pass naturally from wisdom; apathy comes from bodily virtues; she urges us always to associate with such graces; whoever associates with these shall not only converse with God but become his housemate; the arete of rational nature is called friendship and makes those who follow it through God’s knowing friendly with God; in the friendship of arete and the company of knowing, the one who associates is many times among the benefited; some think this concerns external wisdom, which it is not good to linger over due to its deceits; others interpret this concerning vice and not being much toward it; thus it is impossible for a man to completely avoid evil thoughts, but not to linger in them is possible; those he calls embraces; every one who guarantees Christ the friend as justice and truth delivers his own psyche to enemies, those accustomed to fighting men, through friendship with the Savior; friendship is spiritual, knowing of God, by which the saints are called friends of God, as John the Baptist was friend of the bridegroom, Moses and the apostles; no longer, he says, do I call you servants, but friends; do you see struggle and vigilance?

choices.choice: neglect: ἀπόλειψις conveys abandonment or leaving behind, fitting the context of forgetting divine covenant alongside λήθη as secondary failures in knowledge pursuit.
